compiled_state.title: [dso_ci_review/dispatch.py]: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'litellm' on every specialist dispatch in CI
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

Every deep-tier specialist dispatched by `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` (or its runner) in the GitHub Actions `llm-review` job crashes immediately with:

```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'litellm'
```

Observed on PR #52, run 25417143564, job 74551374067 (HEAD `eb26cd7ef9`). Job ran for 5 seconds total and emitted three identical specialist_error findings — one per deep-tier agent (`code-reviewer-deep-correctness`, `code-reviewer-deep-verification`, `code-reviewer-deep-hygiene`).

This is the runtime defect itself, distinct from:
- fcea-6e83-ebad-49af (P0): the runner exits 0 on this error — that bug is about exit-code propagation
- b38d-1781-ef5a-41af (P0): the integration shipped without a functional review able to catch this — that bug is about pre-merge validation gaps

This bug is the WHAT — the actual runtime failure that needs to stop happening.

## Expected Behavior

`dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` runs in CI without raising `ModuleNotFoundError`. Specialists dispatch successfully and produce real findings.

## Actual Behavior

`import litellm` at the top of dispatch.py (or one of its imports) raises `ModuleNotFoundError`. The dispatch wrapper catches it per-specialist and converts it into a `specialist_error` finding. All 3 deep-tier specialists fail identically.

## Evidence

```json
{
  "findings": [
    {"type":"specialist_error","agent_id":"code-reviewer-deep-correctness",
     "severity":"important","category":"correctness",
     "description":"Specialist code-reviewer-deep-correctness failed: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'litellm'",
     "cited_lines":[]},
    {"type":"specialist_error","agent_id":"code-reviewer-deep-verification", "...":"..."},
    {"type":"specialist_error","agent_id":"code-reviewer-deep-hygiene", "...":"..."}
  ],
  "scores": {},
  "summary": ""
}
```

PR: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/52
Job: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/runs/25417143564/job/74551374067

## Affected Paths

- `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` — site of the `import litellm` (or transitive import)
- `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/runner.py` — likely also imports litellm
- `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/config.py` — may also import litellm for provider configuration
- The CI workflow YAML that invokes the runner (likely `.github/workflows/ci-llm-review.yml` or wherever `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` is exec'd) — the install step that should have provisioned `litellm` is missing or broken

## Reproduction

```bash
# Locally, in a clean Python env with no litellm:
python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'plugins/dso/scripts'); from dso_ci_review.dispatch import *"
# Expected post-fix: succeeds (or produces an import path error that is NOT 'litellm')
# Actual today: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'litellm'
```

In CI, the same import fires when the runner attempts to dispatch any specialist.

## Suggested Fix Direction

The fix has two parts:

### Part A — Provision `litellm` in the CI environment (immediate)

Identify the install step the `llm-review` job runs and add `litellm` to it. Candidates (one will be authoritative for this project):

1. `.github/workflows/ci-llm-review.yml` — add `pip install litellm` (or `pip install -r requirements-ci.txt` after adding `litellm` to that file)
2. `pyproject.toml` — add `litellm` to a CI-only optional dependency group (e.g., `[project.optional-dependencies] ci = ["litellm>=X.Y"]`) and the workflow runs `pip install -e .[ci]`
3. `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/requirements.txt` — module-local manifest the runner installs from on entry

Pin to the LiteLLM version verified during local development of the integration. Document the choice in `docs/contracts/` so future updates pass through review.

### Part B — Smoke-import gate before dispatch (defense-in-depth)

At the very top of `ci-llm-review-runner.sh` (before any specialist dispatch and before any heredoc that suppresses errors):

```bash
python3 -c "import litellm; import dso_ci_review.dispatch" || {
    echo "ERROR: ci-llm-review prerequisites missing — 'litellm' not importable" >&2
    echo "Install litellm in the CI environment before re-running this job." >&2
    exit 1
}
```

This guarantees a missing dep fails the job at its earliest opportunity, with a clear error and exit 1 — which (paired with fcea-6e83-ebad-49af) propagates to a red CI check.

### Part C — Regression test

Add a CI test that:
1. Stands up a Python venv with the project's CI requirements installed
2. Runs `python -c "import litellm; from dso_ci_review.dispatch import dispatch_specialist"` and asserts exit 0
3. Runs against a fixture diff and asserts at least one specialist actually executes (not just specialist_error finding)

## Priority Justification (P0)

P0 because:
- Every CI invocation of the deep-tier review tier crashes — 100% failure rate
- Without this, the full deep-tier review pipeline is non-functional even after fcea-6e83-ebad-49af and b38d-1781-ef5a-41af are fixed
- The other two P0s in this trio describe the consequences (silent-pass + ship-without-validation); this one IS the runtime regression that those bugs allowed to land and persist

## Related Tickets

- **fcea-6e83-ebad-49af (P0)** — companion: runner exits 0 on this error (silent-pass)
- **b38d-1781-ef5a-41af (P0)** — companion: integration shipped without functional review able to catch this
- f03f-47d7-298b-46ec (closed) — earlier LiteLLM-related fix (`context_window_fallbacks` parameter); demonstrates the LiteLLM integration is being actively iterated on without its CI gate functioning

## Fix-trio Coordination

These three P0s should be fixed together in one change-set:
1. **This bug** — install `litellm` in CI + add smoke-import gate (the runtime fix)
2. **fcea-6e83-ebad-49af** — propagate non-zero exit on specialist_error (the gate-fidelity fix)
3. **b38d-1781-ef5a-41af** — pre-merge validation that prevents this class of failure from shipping again (the process fix)

Landing only one or two leaves a partial regression: e.g., fixing exit codes without installing litellm produces a constantly-red llm-review check that blocks every PR; fixing the install without exit-code propagation hides any future similar regression behind a green check.
